title: Choose the visual world for the PlusOne landing page
question: The roll assigned The Departures Board. Keep it, take the pick, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departures Board
options.lineage: Solari split-flap boards in station halls
options.thesis: Your wedding as a live departures board: every vendor is a row that flips from searching to sent to quoted while you watch.
options.viewport: Marigold field; left: name, promise and inline sign-up; right: a large board titled Priya & Sam departures whose rows flip as emails send and a quote lands.
options.risk: Can read as travel, not wedding, if the board copy is not unmistakably about vendors and days.

raised.raise: Every price on the board is pinned by a leader line to the page or email it came from.
One sweeping now-line always shows where the plan is, like a chase light.
How-it-works is one orthogonal route map wiring search, email, reply and budget.
The single number that just changed gets a marked highlight, nothing else does.

options.label: The Reply Card
options.lineage: wedding stationery suites: invitation, RSVP card, envelope
options.thesis: PlusOne as the correspondence of the wedding: every vendor email and guest reply set like a stationery suite that fills itself in.
options.viewport: A reply card with its +1 line, the couple's inbox address printed on the envelope, replies arriving as filled-in cards.
options.risk: Closest to the wedding-stationery look most sites in this category already use; can feel familiar.

options.label: Man-Machine Identity
options.thesis: The planning flow as a neon wiring diagram on a strict signal grid.
options.viewport: A black grid with neon connectors routing search to inbox to budget.
options.risk: Neon on black is the generic AI-startup look.
options.case: Declined: you ruled out the generic SaaS look, and couples do not identify with a machine diagram.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.thesis: A friend sketching how PlusOne works on a napkin.
options.viewport: Doodled arrows from a mascot to the inbox.
options.risk: Cutesy mascots undercut trust around money.
options.case: Declined: breaks the warm-not-cutesy voice and your too-playful red line.
options.kept: One highlighter mark on the number that changed.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: The wedding timeline as sixteen lit step keys.
options.viewport: A step row of days with a chase light.
options.risk: Instrument grammar is foreign to couples.
options.case: Declined: low identification and unclear mapping to vendors.
options.kept: A chase-light now-line that always shows where the plan is.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.viewport: A floating column annotated with force values.
options.case: Declined: loses on both identification and clarity.
options.kept: Leader-line annotations pinning each figure to its source.

options.label: Coiled Earth Tower
options.thesis: The plan rising course by course.
options.viewport: A banded tower of planning courses.
options.risk: Earthy craft mood without the product mechanism.
options.kept: Each row keeps a visible trail of its past states.

options.label: Vertical Feed Surface
options.risk: Needs real photography PlusOne does not have.
options.case: Declined: no media to fill it and weak clarity.
options.kept: On phones, one board row owns the screen at a time.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The wedding-platform homepage done at full craft: soft photo hero, app screenshot, feature grid.
canonCard.viewport: Couple photo behind a headline and Get started, product screenshot below, five feature cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Joy and Zola by design.
